newsitem.title: USA: Changes seen coming at U.S. State Dept.
newsitem.headline: Changes seen coming at U.S. State Dept.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher's chief of staff, Tom Donilon, is expected to resign and be replaced by another senior official, James Steinberg, administration officials said on Tuesday.
The top-level changes -- expected to take effect on Monday -- are seen as a prelude to Christopher's own departure, part of the changes that usually accompany election or re-election of a president.

Donilon, a long-time Democratic activist, was a partner in Christopher's law firm, O'Melveny and Myers, before being appointed assistant secretary of state for public affairs at the start of the Clinton adminstration in 1993.
He later was given the title of chief of staff, which better described his close relationship with Christopher and his essential role at the State Department.

Donilon and his wife Catherine Russell recently had their first baby and he is believed to want to spend more time with his family after travelling nearly 700,000 miles (1.127 million km) as Christopher's top aide.
He is expected to take several months off and then take a job in the private sector, officials said.

Steinberg has also been part of Christopher's inner circle as director of the department's policy planning staff. Per an agreement struck in July, Donilon gradually phased out of his chief of staff role with Steinberg assuming more of those responsibilities.

Previously, Steinberg was deputy director of the department's bureau for intelligence and research and a senior analyst at the RAND Corp. A European expert, he also worked for the International Institute for Strategic Studies in London and for Democratic Sen. Edward Kennedy.
A Democratic political activist, he also has been an adviser on national security issues for former Democratic presidential candidate MIchael Dukakis.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns is expected to be named acting assistant secretary of state for public affairs, officials said.
Christopher has not announced his intentions but it is widely expected he will not serve a second four-year term if President Clinton is re-elected Tuesday as predicted.

He was invited to Little Rock, Ark. at the last minute by Clinton for discussions that Burns said would cover a variety of topics. The spokesman did not rule out a conversation with Clinton about Christopher's future.
